claims.text: In single-phase HEAs containing at least five elements at 5 at.% or more each, superconducting transition temperature is governed by average valence electron count.
Increasing average valence electron count while maintaining moderate atomic disorder enhances the density of states at the Fermi level.
An enhanced density of states at the Fermi level strengthens electron-phonon coupling.
Stronger electron-phonon coupling caused by increased average valence electron count raises Tc relative to the baseline alloy.
The proposed baseline is a superconducting, single-phase Nb-Ta-based HEA with known average VEC and moderate atomic disorder.
Partial substitution with higher-valence elements can incrementally increase average VEC while preserving the single-phase structure and moderate disorder.
Local atomic arrangement sets the effective density of states at the Fermi level.
The density of states at the Fermi level mediates electron-phonon interactions.
Incrementally VEC-increased HEAs maintained at moderate disorder will have a higher Tc than the baseline alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the HEA remains a single-phase solid solution with controlled atomic disorder.
Excessive atomic disorder may cause electron localization.
Electron localization caused by excessive disorder may suppress superconductivity.
Failure of Tc to increase, or a decrease in Tc, as VEC increases under maintained single-phase and moderate-disorder conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
